items.summary: AnyLanguageModel 1.0, alongside swift-huggingface 1.0 and swift-xet 1.0, expands Apple's local and hosted inference capabilities. The update introduces guided generation, tool calling, and image support across providers. It now supports models like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google's Gemini, plus private cloud compute on OS 27. Developers can use open-weight models too large for devices via Inference Providers, while local models remain accessible on iOS, macOS, and visionOS.
items.title: AnyLanguageModel 1.0 Unveils New Local and Hosted Inference Features

items.summary: Google Cloud reported that services are recovering following a power event at its London data centre that disrupted UK banks, businesses, and courts. While banks did not directly link the issues to Google, the company apologised and confirmed recovery. Revolut and Lloyds Banking Group also reported disruptions, with Lloyds stating root issues are resolved. Experts note the incident highlights reliance on major cloud providers.
items.title: Google Cloud Services Recover After UK Outage Hits Banks

items.summary: Federal prosecutors revealed that former OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan was nearly arrested while planning to flee to Saudi Arabia. He is charged with installing a recording device in an executive conference room. A federal judge denied his request for home confinement, citing his ties to a foreign government and ample resources. His next court date is scheduled for November.
items.title: Former OpenAI Engineer Accused of Bugging Conference Room Faces Detention

items.summary: The U.S. Department of Homeland Security ordered federal civilian agencies to stop using DeepSeek products and remove them from government systems due to security risks and concerns about Chinese government access. The order covers affiliates and derivatives, requiring immediate removal or exception requests within 60 days. CISA will review requests, while the ban does not affect private or consumer use.
items.title: DHS Bans DeepSeek Products in Federal Civilian Agencies

items.summary: The U.S. ordered federal civilian agencies to stop purchasing and remove DeepSeek AI from government systems due to national security concerns. The Department of Homeland Security warned that sensitive data could be accessible to Chinese authorities. China pushed back, calling the move an overstretching of security concepts. The order extends previous restrictions on intelligence agencies to civilian departments.
items.title: US Orders Federal Agencies to Remove Chinese AI Startup DeepSeek

items.summary: The US government ordered agencies to stop using DeepSeek AI tools on Monday. The Department of Homeland Security announced the ban, citing threats from servers located in China where authorities can access private infrastructure. The DHS noted that using these tools may transfer sensitive data to China. While the ban applies to civilian agencies, the military and intelligence services were not included. The US defense department did not respond to a request for comment.
items.title: US Bans DeepSeek AI Tools for Government Agencies Amid Security Concerns

items.summary: The UK Competition and Markets Authority is consulting on proposals to require Apple to lower fees and widen access to its contactless payment technology. The regulator argues current restrictions block innovation, citing that nearly 60% of UK users employ digital wallets. While Apple maintains its security standards prevent barriers, the CMA contends opening access to Host Card Emulation would foster new businesses and services in the UK's fintech sector.
items.title: UK watchdog urges Apple to lower fees and widen payment access

items.summary: Amber Sinha reports that India's constitutional right to peaceful assembly is being undermined by a preemptive policing strategy utilizing digital surveillance and mass detention. Since June, thousands have protested for voting rights, but on October 10, over 5,000 people were detained in New Delhi ahead of a demonstration. Intelligence units tracked 200 messaging groups and compiled databases of 500 organizers and 100 reporters. Law enforcement deployed 35,000 security personnel supported by facial recognition systems and signal-jamming equipment. The Delhi Metro closed 57 stations, and Jantar Mantar was denotified as a protest site. Sinha argues this shifts the burden of proof onto citizens, treating protest as a security threat rather than a democratic right. The Supreme Court recently reviewed challenges but offered limited relief, leaving the executive's surveillance apparatus largely unchecked.
items.title: India Faces Preemptive Policing Crackdown on Protesters Amid Digital Surveillance

items.summary: Edward Robinson, chief economist at the Monetary Authority of Singapore, stated that central banks might ease monetary policy once artificial intelligence delivers widespread productivity gains. However, he advised keeping policy restrictive for now due to demand from the AI investment boom. Robinson noted that while AI is diffusing quickly, significant economy-wide efficiency improvements have not yet materialized.
items.title: MAS Economist Says AI Productivity Gains Could Ease Monetary Policy

items.summary: At the PyTorch Conference North America, llm-d project contributors announced version 1.0, marking a major milestone for open-source AI infrastructure. Developed by Red Hat, IBM, Google, and others, this Kubernetes-native system enables distributed inference across various models, accelerators, and clouds. The release focuses on production readiness, offering sustained efficiency, multi-tenant support, and zero-downtime operations. By integrating techniques like prefix-cache-aware routing, llm-d aims to reduce costs and improve ROI for enterprises deploying AI at scale, providing a vendor-neutral alternative to proprietary solutions.
items.title: llm-d 1.0 Brings Open-Source AI Inference to Production Readiness

items.summary: Taobao is investing 100 million yuan in Singapore promotions for its 11.11 Singles' Day sale launching Oct 20. The investment covers free shipping vouchers, physical advertising on 200 big screens, and shopping vouchers. Cora Cai, Taobao's Singapore country head, stated the spending is double that of the 2025 season as part of the company's expansion efforts in the region.
items.title: Taobao Invests Millions in Singapore Promotions for 11.11 Sale

items.summary: River John Lim Jit Nong submitted a forum post urging authorities to permit songbirds in covered cages on buses and MRT trains. The author argues that for many senior enthusiasts, these birds are treasured companions essential for social connection and active ageing. Lim suggests the rule would preserve a unique tradition while helping seniors remain socially engaged during their journeys.
items.title: Forum Proposal Allows Songbirds in Cages on Public Transport

items.summary: Transient Workers Count Too (TWC2) welcomes the National Wages Council's recommendation for a 6% to 8% pay rise for lower-wage workers but urges employers to include migrant workers. TWC2 notes that current guidelines exclude these workers from wage models like the Progressive Wage Model. The group highlights that many work permit holders earn low wages, with marine shipyard workers averaging $567. TWC2 calls for reporting on guideline adoption for foreign employees.
items.title: TWC2 Urges Inclusion of Migrant Workers in Wage Recommendations

items.summary: CustomerLake announced that Campaign Agents has advanced to Beta and Profile Agents has entered Private Preview, marking a new stage of maturity for its Agentic CDP embedded in Databricks. The update expands participation to more enterprises, including HP, Getnet by Santander, AB InBev, and Wine.com, which report faster audience turnaround times and reduced costs. For instance, HP noted a potential 40% reduction in CDP total cost of ownership, while Philadelphia Union reported a 90% cut in audience turnaround time. These features aim to provide marketers with trusted customer context and autonomous capabilities directly within their existing data platforms.
items.title: CustomerLake Advances Agentic CDP Features to Beta and Private Preview

items.summary: TechScape editor Blake Montgomery reports on the dangers of tech billionaires shaping global infrastructure and culture. The segment highlights Elon Musk's SpaceX as the world's largest satellite operator, noting its critical role in Ukraine's war efforts and recent service restrictions. It also covers musicians like A$AP Rocky and Grimes expressing caution toward AI-generated music, alongside fan preferences for analog sounds. Finally, the report features a Guardian conference in Paris where experts discussed resisting AI's creep by choosing to be more human, with Naomi Klein warning of a fascist future driven by centralized knowledge.
items.title: Tech Billionaire Influence and AI Concerns Discussed

items.summary: ZDNET reports that a recent October Windows 11 update disables Smart App Control, a security feature added in 2022. Microsoft states it is working on a fix. Users can temporarily restore the feature by adding specific keys to the Windows Registry and rebooting their PC.
items.title: Microsoft Windows Update Disables Smart App Control Feature

items.summary: Figma announced 20 new Model Context Protocol partners at its India Config conference, expanding support for the open-source standard. Co-founder Dylan Field expressed concerns that MCP is not a perfect protocol and favors frontier labs. He noted risks of data abuse if Figma fully exposes data through MCP, though the company remains committed to opening its ecosystem.
items.title: Figma Expands MCP Support Despite Co-Founder Concerns

items.summary: The Romanian government and Nuclearelectrica cannot restart the Cernavodă nuclear plant until the Danube recovers from record-low water levels. An interministerial committee issued a report recommending sophisticated cooling systems for current and future reactors. The shutdown complicates restart efforts, while water diversion measures have limited shipping. Profit.ro reported that Nuclearelectrica lowered its 2026 profit projection by 43% to RON 1.18 billion, assuming a restart by November 1.
items.title: Romania seeks better cooling for Cernavodă nuclear plant

items.summary: Countries failed to agree on a timeline for the IPCC's seventh assessment report at its 65th session in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, marking the sixth consecutive failure to reach consensus. The meeting, intended to set a schedule for reports to inform the UN's 2028 global stocktake, descended into disagreements between nations wanting reports published by 2028 and those seeking delays. IPCC Chair Prof Sir Jim Skea suspended the talks on Friday evening after delegates could not agree on a draft decision or the IPCC's budget, leaving the body in a "serious funding crisis." While scientists pledged to continue drafting the reports, the breakdown has raised concerns that the lack of agreement could undermine global climate action and the IPCC's ability to deliver timely scientific advice.
items.title: IPCC Meeting Ends in Disarray Over Report Timeline and Funding

items.summary: BYD has launched the second-generation Seagull EV in China, positioning it as its most affordable electric vehicle. Starting at 62,900 yuan with a promotion, the model features 5-minute Flash Charging and rear-wheel drive. The vehicle offers two battery options with ranges up to 420 km and includes upgraded interior technology and smart driving assistance systems.
items.title: BYD Launches Affordable Seagull EV with Fast Charging

items.summary: Record-high shipping costs driven by the Iran war and Strait of Hormuz disruptions are forcing Asian crude buyers to switch to smaller tankers and Middle Eastern supplies. This shift has shut U.S. Gulf Coast arbitrage, while European refiners opt for regional volumes. Premiums on European and Middle Eastern grades have spiked, whereas discounts on African and U.S. crudes have widened due to high freight costs.
items.title: Record Freight Costs Force Asian Buyers to Use Smaller Tankers

items.summary: Mexican authorities announced the rollback of 2020 protections for the vaquita, the world's rarest marine mammal, citing the need to support local fishing communities in San Felipe. The move reduces prohibited gillnet areas by 86 percent and opens a vessel transit corridor in the Sea of Cortez. While conservationists warn this could lead to extinction, local officials defend the decision as essential for economic survival. Some fishermen remain dissatisfied, blocking roads over the retention of the 'Zero Tolerance Area.' The government faces pressure to balance conservation with the livelihoods of 17,000 residents.
items.title: Mexico Reduces Vaquita Protections Amid Local Fishing Tensions

items.summary: Sarajevo Canton authorities introduced the first subsidies for businesses to reduce air pollution, expanding previous measures that covered households and public buildings. The EUR 500,000 fund supports replacing solid fuel stoves and boilers in commercial premises. Prime Minister Nihad Uk and Minister Mladen Pandurević stated the program aims to modernize facilities and mitigate restrictive winter measures. Applications will be issued soon.
items.title: Sarajevo launches subsidies for business air pollution reduction

items.summary: A fleet of 74 electric school buses in Oakland, California, powers approximately 1,000 homes and generates revenue through vehicle-to-grid technology. Operated by Zum with chargers built by Tellus Power, the buses discharge energy during peak demand periods, such as late afternoons and summer holidays. Over the last two years, the fleet returned 1.7GWh of energy to the grid with over 99.5% uptime. The California Energy Commission estimates that widespread V2H adoption could save homeowners money and cut peak demand by up to 5GW statewide. Tellus notes that its chargers enable faster deployment compared to traditional power plants.
items.title: Oakland School Buses Power Homes and Generate Revenue via V2G

items.summary: Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov visited Iran on October 19 to discuss strategic partnership, occurring amid questions regarding Moscow's support for Tehran in its conflict with the United States. US President Donald Trump claimed on October 18 that Russia provides little to no assistance. Conversely, analyst Hamidreza Azizi stated that Russian support has been tangible, citing intelligence aiding precision strikes. Experts note Russia shares satellite imagery and signals intelligence while avoiding direct conflict. A senior EU official described Trump's comments as propaganda to explain softness on Russia. The visit emphasized strengthening ties without mentioning military cooperation publicly.
items.title: Russia's Support for Iran in War Faces Scrutiny Amid Lavrov Visit

items.summary: Alphabet's Google announced on Tuesday that full service has been restored in its London-based cloud region. The company stated the outage was caused by a power event that previously disrupted multiple cloud services. This update follows the incident, confirming operational normalcy for the affected infrastructure.
items.title: Google Cloud Services Restored in London After Power Event

items.summary: Liz argues that AI companies defy the rule of not fighting the Federal Reserve, borrowing more even as rates rise. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee notes inflation is spreading from AI sectors. While Warsh at the IMF in Bangkok acknowledges a price shock, he expects future wealth. The article suggests these tech leaders prioritize existential goals over borrowing costs, risking public anger if mortgages reach 15% while they spend freely.
items.title: AI Giants Ignore Fed Rate Hikes Amid Inflation Concerns

items.summary: On October 20, Apple announced a commitment to purchase up to $100 million worth of titanium over three years from a Pennsylvania-based supplier. This purchase is part of Apple's American Manufacturing Program, aimed at expanding domestic production. The agreement covers titanium for various products, including the upcoming iPhone Duo, and supports Apple's broader strategy to increase manufacturing within the United States.
items.title: Apple Commits $100 Million for US Titanium Manufacturing

items.summary: The US banned Chinese AI firm DeepSeek from most government systems and ordered agencies to remove technology built with it. This move occurs as competition for AI supremacy between the superpowers intensifies. While US firms accuse Chinese rivals of malicious exploitation, researchers urge Washington and Beijing to collaborate on regulating the technology, which some warn poses an existential threat to humanity.
items.title: US Bans DeepSeek From Government Systems Amid AI Competition

items.summary: A Google cloud failure in the UK knocked offline courts and banks including Lloyds, HSBC, and Revolut, affecting millions. Google attributed the issue to a power event in its London operations. Services resumed by 3pm, though legal proceedings and financial transactions faced delays. Regulators and affected firms confirmed the disruption and are monitoring the situation.
items.title: Google Cloud Outage Disrupts UK Courts and Banks

items.summary: The Nasdaq declined between 0.4% and 0.5%, with AI-linked stocks like Micron, Intel, and Sandisk falling about 2%. Investors expressed unease over the sustainability of the AI trade, citing concerns about excessive corporate debt funding build-outs. CoreWeave stock dropped more than 3% as scrutiny focused on its data center financing.
items.title: Nasdaq Slips as AI Stocks Fall Amid Debt Worries

items.summary: Citrini Research utilized the AI model Claude to design 211 proteins for lab testing, with 17 successfully binding to scorpion toxins. The firm identified Revvity, Charles River Laboratories, and Tecan Group as top stock picks, citing growing AI adoption in biotech. Citrini noted that while the proteins bind targets, blocking effects remain untested, and significant scientific work is required before any treatment results can be claimed.
items.title: Citrini Research Uses AI to Design Proteins for Life Sciences Stocks

items.summary: Court records indicate that TikTok executives failed to act on repeated internal warnings from staff regarding child safety risks, including sexual exploitation and suicide content. Employees reported that leadership was aware of these dangers but did not prioritize fixes. The documents, from depositions filed in March 2026, highlight concerns about minors accessing harmful content and bypassing age restrictions. TikTok declined to comment on the allegations. The company is a defendant in multi-district litigation alleging its platform is designed to harm users under 18.
items.title: Court Records Reveal TikTok Executives Ignored Child Safety Warnings

items.summary: Nithin Kamath, founder of Zerodha, stated that relying on stock tips from WhatsApp, Telegram, SMS, and social media is the silliest way to lose money, noting this trend persists even in 2026. He warned that such instances are likely to increase and urged investors to use AI assistants like Claude or ChatGPT to verify investment ideas before acting on them.
items.title: Nithin Kamath Warns Against WhatsApp Stock Tips in 2026

items.summary: Flutter Entertainment announced plans to cut up to 1,400 jobs, attributing the move to tax increases on online casino and sports betting. CEO Kevin Harrington stated the hikes fundamentally changed the industry's economic model. The company reported a $299m pre-tax loss for the three months to June, contrasting with a $205m profit the previous year. Flutter also noted revenues in the UK and Ireland rose by 4%.
items.title: Flutter cuts 1,400 jobs citing gambling tax rises

items.summary: The Unite union opposes NatWest's plan to require 30,000 employees to attend the office at least two days weekly starting February. The bank cites collaboration benefits, while Unite argues the move increases costs for lower-paid staff and ignores childcare needs. NatWest will support a transition period for affected workers.
items.title: Unite Union Criticizes NatWest Plan to Reduce Remote Work Rights

items.summary: Ryanair chief executive Michael O’Leary predicts European air fares could rise by as much as 20% in 2027, citing soaring jet fuel costs driven by the Middle East conflict. He notes many carriers lack hedging against these costs, warning of potential bankruptcies and takeovers. O’Leary highlighted that while some airlines have hedged for 2026, most remain exposed from April 2027 onwards, with fuel prices currently hovering at double the hedged rates.
items.title: Ryanair Boss Predicts Major European Air Fare Hike

items.summary: Bollywood actors Deepika Padukone and Ranveer Singh announced the name of their second daughter, Devi Padukone Singh, on October 20. They shared a family photograph featuring themselves, their elder daughter Dua, and the newborn on Instagram to mark Dussehra. The image showed the family in coordinated ivory and golden traditional outfits.
items.title: Deepika Padukone and Ranveer Singh Reveal Second Daughter's Name

items.summary: A power outage at a Google Cloud data centre in London caused serious network disruptions to services on Tuesday, according to the US tech giant. The incident affected multiple Google Cloud services, impacting UK banks like Revolut, Lloyds, and HSBC. Google stated a full recovery was expected by 1300 GMT, while other businesses also reported issues.
items.title: Power Outage at Google Cloud Data Centre Disrupts UK Banking Services

items.summary: A study by the University of Bath indicates that providing unconditional cash transfers to Indigenous communities in the Peruvian Amazon contributes to rainforest protection. The two-year pilot project, managed by Cool Earth, gave 211 people in Peru's Asháninka region roughly £2 a day. Researchers found that 90% of participants adopted environmentally beneficial practices, while food insecurity and forced migration decreased significantly. However, the authors note the study's small scale and limited ecological measurements, calling for wider research.
items.title: Study finds cash aid helps protect Amazon rainforest

items.summary: The annual Orionid meteor shower is expected to peak on the night of October 21 to 22, 2025. NASA notes that around 20 meteors may be seen per hour under ideal conditions. The event is created by debris from Comet 1P/Halley. Observers are advised to avoid city lights and allow eyes to adjust to darkness.
items.title: NASA and astronomers forecast Orionid meteor shower peak

items.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping emphasized that green development is essential to high-quality growth while inspecting Ulanqab in Inner Mongolia. He urged the country to prioritize ecological conservation and pursue green growth. The region is leveraging its ecological and energy advantages, transforming them into new drivers of growth through projects like wetland restoration and developing a global green computing hub.
items.title: Xi Jinping Urges Green Growth During Inner Mongolia Inspection

items.summary: An exceptionally strong El Niño is combining with human-caused climate change to drive extreme weather globally. The phenomenon contributes to record heat, droughts, and wildfires, while also threatening coral reefs and forests. In El Salvador, drought has left cattle starving, and heavy rains in Argentina have forced evacuations. UN officials warn that the event, amplified by warming, could push millions into poverty and undermine economic recovery in places like Sri Lanka. Scientists note that while the current event is very strong, its historical ranking depends on measurement methods and will be confirmed only after it ends.
items.title: El Niño and Climate Change Drive Global Extreme Weather

items.summary: The Hind Rajab Foundation urges the US to arrest Sean Glass, an Israeli commander, linking him to the 2024 killing of 5-year-old Hind Rajab in Gaza. The group alleges Glass likely ordered the firing that killed Hind and two paramedics, citing evidence of 335 bullets fired at her vehicle. Representative Rashida Tlaib supports the call for an investigation into the alleged war crimes and genocide.
items.title: Rights Group Urges US Arrest of Israeli Commander Linked to Gaza Killing

items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met with senior US envoys in Norway to discuss stalled military aid, accusing the Pentagon of delaying interceptor missiles and withholding intelligence. Relations have soured following US President Donald Trump's criticism of Zelenskyy and sanctions relief for Russia. While the US denies deliberately withholding supplies, Zelenskyy insists on restoring the Starshield satellite system and receiving ballistic missile interceptors to protect against ongoing Russian attacks.
items.title: Zelenskyy Meets US Envoys Amid Sinking Relations Over Missile Aid

items.summary: Sources accuse Sudan's army of launching drone strikes that killed more than 200 people, including mourners and market attendees in West Kordofan and Abyei. The Sudan War Observatory reports 150 deaths in West Kordofan and 73 in Abyei. A military source claims the market in Abyei was a fuel supply site for the RSF. South Sudan has lodged a formal protest. The conflict has created a severe humanitarian crisis, displacing over 14 million people and leaving 20 million facing acute hunger. The UN expresses alarm over the continued deadly strikes.
items.title: Sudan Army Accused of Drone Strikes Killing Hundreds

items.summary: T-shirts bearing the slogan 'Tinubu Must Go!' are at the center of an escalating crackdown on dissent in Nigeria's north. Police in Borno arrested five men for wearing them, alleging conspiracy to breach public peace, while authorities in Kano blocked access to a planned meeting of the same movement. Human rights groups and activists criticize these actions as an assault on freedom of expression and democracy. The incidents highlight concerns over the thin line between legitimate security measures and political dissent, especially as Nigeria faces severe economic crises and pervasive insecurity. Critics argue that the government is suppressing opposition voices ahead of the 2027 presidential election.
items.title: Nigeria's Northern Protests Test Limits of Political Dissent

items.summary: Indigenous People's Minister Eloy Terena warns that achievements made since 2023 could be undone if Flávio Bolsonaro becomes Brazil's president. Terena states Bolsonaro might abolish the ministry and stop land demarcations. Philosopher Ailton Krenak fears Bolsonaro would corrupt management of federal bodies defending Indigenous interests. Flávio Bolsonaro, who received 47.03% of the vote, promised not to demarcate Indigenous lands and plans to review federal agencies. The Ministry of Indigenous Peoples was created in January 2023 by President Lula. Terena and Krenak express concern about potential policy reversals and threats to Indigenous rights under a Bolsonaro administration.
items.title: Brazilian Indigenous Minister Warns of Risks if Flávio Bolsonaro Wins Presidency

items.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky traveled to Oslo to meet US envoys, aiming to restore diplomatic relations strained by Washington's alleged delay in delivering interceptor missiles. Zelensky accused the US of withholding intelligence and military aid, specifically citing a lack of early warning for Russian missile strikes. Conversely, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio denied deliberate denial of supplies, citing a balance of obligations. US President Donald Trump also criticized Zelensky, suggesting he should not negotiate. Meanwhile, Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store confirmed the talks, which included Finnish President Alexander Stubb and US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. The meeting seeks to place diplomatic efforts on a more constructive path.
items.title: Zelensky Meets US Envoys in Oslo Amid Missile Delivery Dispute

items.summary: Local authorities in Yemen's Shabwa province report that a Houthi missile strike killed 73 security recruits at a training camp. Initial reports cited 53 deaths, but an investigative committee later updated the toll to 73 with 14 missing. The government condemned the attack as a war crime, while Houthi officials claimed the target was a Saudi military concentration. Fighting continues across Yemen as the conflict escalates.
items.title: Houthi Missile Strike Kills 73 Yemen Security Recruits

items.summary: Ethiopia's Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed warned Eritrea on Monday that it faces severe consequences if it continues to support rebels in his country. The warning follows a recent offensive by Tigray rebels backed by Eritrea, which were forced to retreat after drone attacks. Abiy stated that serving as a base for enemies brings no benefits and emphasized that good neighbourly relations are the only way forward.
items.title: Ethiopia PM Warns Eritrea Over Support for Rebels

items.title: Argentine President Visits Spain Amid Snap Elections

items.summary: A study of 24 final-year student teachers in South Africa reveals that university training programmes often fail to prepare educators to challenge social inequality. While most participants engaged in technical reflection focused on classroom management, only five demonstrated critical reflection regarding poverty and language policy. The research attributes this gap largely to mentor teachers who prioritized routine compliance over deep discussion. Consequently, the study warns that without encouraging critical examination of social realities, future teachers may simply adapt to existing inequalities rather than reducing them, risking the reproduction of an unequal society.
items.title: South African Teacher Training Fails to Challenge Inequality

items.summary: A study by the International Centre for Taxation and Development and Redefine in Tanzania reveals that the presence of tax officials during surveys did not uniformly build trust. While visibility strengthened trust in wealthier regions like Dar es Salaam, it reduced trust and tax payments in poorer areas such as Mtwara and Kigoma. The research, based on a trial with 1,210 small businesses across 119 wards, suggests that light-touch outreach fails to automatically build credibility where state presence is otherwise thin. Instead, authorities must diagnose local trust levels and design outreach to suit specific contexts, ensuring that visibility is paired with perceived fairness and service delivery.
items.title: Study Finds Tax Official Visits Can Erode Trust in Poorer Tanzanian Regions

items.summary: China criticized the United States ban on DeepSeek's products in federal civilian agencies, arguing Washington is politicizing technology. The Department of Homeland Security ordered agencies to remove DeepSeek and related products from IT systems, citing security threats. Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning stated China will safeguard its companies' rights and opposes the politicization of science and trade.
items.title: China Criticizes US Ban on DeepSeek AI in Federal Agencies

items.summary: Apple confirmed a product launch event titled 'Pro and Tell' in Los Angeles on October 28. The company plans to debut its first touch-screen MacBook Pro, alongside a new low-end model with an M6 chip, a refreshed iMac, and a revamped iPad mini. Bloomberg News reported these introductions, noting the event marks a major reversal for Apple regarding its previous stance on combining iPad and Mac experiences.
items.title: Apple Announces Touch-Screen MacBook Pro Launch Event

items.summary: A 43-year-old Nagpur accountant lost Rs 1.30 crore after scammers spoofed his employer's WhatsApp profile. On October 16, 2026, the victim transferred funds to a Dahisar bank account based on fraudulent instructions. The deception was revealed when the real employer questioned the unauthorized transaction. Police are investigating the mule account and tracing the perpetrators behind the digital spoofing.
items.title: Nagpur Accountant Loses 1.30 Crore to WhatsApp Scammers

items.summary: A Google Cloud outage disrupted banking services in the UK on Tuesday, affecting Revolut Ltd., Lloyds Banking Group Plc, HSBC, and Royal Bank of Scotland. Google reported issues in its London region but offered no cause, advising customers to migrate services if feasible. Revolut confirmed a service disruption while assuring that customer funds and data remain safe. The incident highlights risks associated with concentrated cloud provider reliance.
items.title: Google Cloud Outage Disrupts Banking Services Across the UK

items.summary: Cognizant and Google Cloud announced an expanded partnership to accelerate agentic AI adoption, creating a new Gemini Frontier Capability Group. Supported by over 18,000 Cognizant associates, the group combines Google's AI platform with Cognizant's expertise to help enterprises deploy production-grade agents. Leaders Ravi Kumar S and Thomas Kurian highlighted the initiative's focus on bridging the gap between pilot projects and scalable business value.
items.title: Cognizant and Google Cloud Expand Partnership for Agentic AI

items.summary: The article explains that Dussehra, or Vijayadashami, marks the triumph of good over evil, celebrated differently across India. While many honor Lord Rama's victory over Ravana, Eastern regions focus on Goddess Durga defeating Mahishasura. It offers curated greetings for family, friends, and colleagues for the 2026 festival, emphasizing positivity and professional warmth. The piece is written by Sounak Mukhopadhyay of LiveMint.
items.title: Dussehra 2026 Wishes and Cultural Context

items.summary: Federal prosecutors arrested Abdulrahman Alfozan, a former OpenAI engineer, on October 9 for planting a sophisticated recording device in an executive conference room. Investigators allege he planned to install additional devices and was in contact with a Saudi royal family member who urged him to relocate to Riyadh. Alfozan, a permanent US resident, was denied bail due to flight risk concerns. He was scheduled to leave for Saudi Arabia with his family shortly after his arrest. The Department of Justice cites his alleged connections to the Saudi government as a national security threat.
items.title: Former OpenAI Engineer Arrested for Planting Recording Device Amid Saudi Ties

items.summary: US President Donald Trump issued a 60-day waiver of sanctions and tariffs linked to Russian oil, aiming to secure national interests and support ongoing trade negotiations with India. Analysts suggest the move is primarily intended to stabilize global oil prices rather than act as a permanent gift to Moscow. While the waiver provides immediate relief for Indian refiners and exporters by removing the threat of 100% tariffs, experts caution that the measure is temporary. With Middle Eastern supplies rising and geopolitical risks persisting, India faces continued uncertainty regarding long-term energy security and potential future US policy shifts.
items.title: Trump's 60-Day Tariff Waiver Offers Temporary Relief to India on Russian Oil

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that India and the US are very close to finalizing a trade agreement, with only a few items remaining. Speaking during his second official visit to India, Rubio expressed optimism that a deal would be announced soon, noting the State Department's involvement in the process.
items.title: Marco Rubio Optimistic on India-US Trade Deal Progress

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed Dushehra celebrations in East Delhi, invoking the ideals of 'Ram Rajya' to emphasize public welfare, social justice, and self-reliance. He stated that the purpose of power is to serve people rather than rule them, prioritizing the needs of the poor and marginalized. Modi highlighted India's cultural heritage and urged the nation to rely on its own resources to achieve a developed and self-reliant future.
items.title: PM Modi Invokes Ram Rajya Ideals at Dussehra Event

items.summary: Former Tamil Nadu BJP president K Annamalai criticized the continued judicial custody of Cockroach Janata Party leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, questioning Delhi Police's handling of the case. Meanwhile, CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke defended the leaders, alleging that their detention and court delays undermine Prime Minister Narendra Modi's strength. A Delhi court extended their custody by two days for alleged violations at Jantar Mantar.
items.title: Annamalai Criticizes Custody of CJP Leaders While Dipke Defends Them

items.summary: Marco Rubio returned to India in 2026 for his second visit, aiming to strengthen economic engagement despite strained relations over tariffs, immigration, and regional conflicts. Both sides indicate progress on a proposed bilateral trade deal, with negotiations nearing a final stage. Discussions will focus on enhancing the India-US strategic partnership and addressing national security waivers related to Russian oil purchases.
items.title: Rubio Returns to India as Trade Deal Nears

items.summary: Jio Platforms opens its IPO with a reserved share pool of up to Rs 2,500 crore for eligible Reliance Industries shareholders. Eligible investors, including individuals and HUFs holding RIL shares as of October 14, 2026, can apply under both shareholder and retail categories to maximize allotment chances. The total IPO raises up to Rs 30,213 crore, with shares priced between Rs 1,065 and Rs 1,119. While applying for larger quantities may improve allocation under the proportionate mechanism, allotment is not guaranteed due to potential oversubscription. Grey market prices indicate a premium of around Rs 245 on October 20.
items.title: Jio IPO Opens with Shareholder Quota and Allotment Rules

items.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari visited bereaved families following the Kolkata stampede that killed 19 people and injured 25. He distributed Rs 25 lakh compensation cheques to each family. Adhikari announced tighter safety measures and requested a judicial probe, while criticizing the previous government for continuing celebrations during the tenure of former chief minister Mamata Banerjee. He also warned of legal action against those spreading false accounts of the incident on social media.
items.title: West Bengal Chief Minister Visits Families After Kolkata Stampede

items.summary: Air Chief Marshal AP Singh flew his final sortie in an HJT-16 Kiran Mk-1 trainer aircraft near Hyderabad on Tuesday, days before his October 31 retirement. The flight, lasting 55 minutes, marked a reunion with his alma mater, the Air Force Academy in Dundigal, and his first instructor, Wing Commander V S Kochar. Singh, who began his flying journey in January 1984, described the event as a 'dream come true' and a completion of a circle. Kochar, 73, called Singh the 'brightest pupil ever.' Singh received a water cannon salute upon landing.
items.title: IAF Chief Flies Final Sortie in Kiran Aircraft Before Retirement

items.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari directed Left parties to sell books from their offices rather than at Durga Puja stalls, citing alleged opposition to Hindu traditions. His comments intensified a dispute following allegations of vandalism against Left party bookstalls and criticism of the party's response to the Chorbagan stampede. Adhikari stated that those who do not accept Vedas or Hindu traditions should not sell books during the festival.
items.title: West Bengal Chief Minister Adhikari Orders Left Parties to Move Book Sales to Offices

items.summary: A 78-year-old woman in Mumbai lost ₹5.85 crore in a cyber fraud involving a fake HDFC Bank insurance policy. Scammers, posing as officials, demanded payments under various pretexts between December 2023 and October 2026. The victim transferred ₹5,85,74,004 before discovering the policy did not exist. Police have registered a case against the suspects.
items.title: Elderly Mumbai Woman Loses Crores in Fake Insurance Scam

items.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari stated that Left parties should sell books from their offices rather than at Durga Puja stalls. His remarks followed allegations that CPI(M) and other Left parties' bookstalls were vandalized during the festival. Adhikari criticized the parties for opposing Sanatani Hindu traditions and suggested Marxist philosophy books be available at their offices, noting they have around 4,000 to 5,000 offices in the state.
items.title: Suvendu says Left parties should sell books from offices, not Durga Puja stalls

items.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio hailed India as a powerful nation during a Mumbai visit, stating that India-US relations will define the 21st century. He noted India is the most populous nation and an oldest democracy, emphasizing the region's pivotal role in shaping the future.
items.title: US Secretary Rubio praises India-US ties as defining for the 21st century

items.summary: US President Donald Trump jokingly proposed renaming New Mexico to New America, suggesting the state change its name to reflect American identity. Senator Ben Ray Lujan responded that the state's name has historical significance dating back centuries. Senator Bernie Sanders criticized the proposal, urging Trump to focus on ending the Iran War instead. The article notes constitutional and legislative obstacles to renaming, highlighting that state constitutions govern such changes. Historical context reveals that America was named after Amerigo Vespucci, not Christopher Columbus, and many indigenous names predate European settlement.
items.title: Trump Jokes About Renaming New Mexico Sparks Debate
